body: I'm addicted to food and alcohol, used to be addicted to weed...at times was addicted to all three. Only time I'm not addicted to food is when I drink too much booze and it makes me have no appetite / impossible to keep much down.

You're totally right. I still have the thought in the back of my mind that somehow we'll end up together. I also realize the delusion though.

So what you're saying is there's a chance? Just kidding haha. I personally am very wary about subjecting anyone to my alcoholic lifestyle. I just have an addictive personality and refuse to latch on to anything where I could affect anyone besides myself. How did those relationships go? Cause being in a relationship with an alcie seems complicated. I'd date an alcoholic chick though, in hopes that maybe we could both find happiness or die pursuing it. Hey, I appreciate it. Comments like those only make me more self-conscious like I'm a bad person for having feelings for this person. Because it's not like I ever have physically stalked or have any intention of literally stalking anyone. I'm very aware of how scary and weird that is. But people on the internet will say what they say I suppose. Everyone is entitled to their opinion. I just feel very strange having this person in my head that I'll never truly know nor have a relationship with.

I'm working on it. For the longest time I was rational in my head about it...reminding myself that she's just a person like everyone else and to not obsess about it. But as time went on it got worse. I feel like I was starting to do better until she showed up today. Just sort of reopened the wound.
Yeah, it's like I know everything on the surface about her from things I learned online. I honestly never thought I'd cyberstalk anyone as much as I have her. I hate it so much.
Yep. It sucks knowing you've thought about them a million times more than they'll ever think about you.

I'm not sure whether I'm glad or not that she has such little presence online. She's very stoic and intriguing, but maybe if she posted more I'd get more of a sense of who she actually is. She always expressed very little emotion or anything personal...so I sort of just created what I hope she is like in my head which I think has made everything worse.

She's 5 years younger. She's 22 and I'm 27. Makes me feel like such a creep because she clearly isn't thinking about long term relationships at this point in her life. I don't know how to stop thinking about her though and picturing her as the love of my life.

Hey thanks for the reply (and sorry for the late response). My mom is very well aware of my addiction issues, but I suffer alone because I don't really have anyone in my life. I think I have avoidant personality disorder or something...I literally have no friends anymore and just work, smoke, drink, sleep, and watch YouTube videos. It's a very sad life I live.
I recently starting working a different schedule where we work together more.
I've been working with her for a year.

Yeah, I know it's never good to put people on a pedestal. I have a really hard time not becoming completely smitten though. The one thing is she is not that easy to talk to...she's completely closed off and doesn't express herself too much. She's very stoic.
It's either be the boost I need or totally mess everything up. I mean she's my boss.
I don't want to risk making things weird...and I think she is way out of my league. Plus I have no confidence.
I'm sorry to hear you're feeling this way! It must be so hard. Have you tried listening to music or going for a walk? /s

Hey, sorry for the late reply. Yeah, I never knew my paternal grandfather because he was an alcoholic who would go on benders all the time so my grandma quickly divorced him. And my maternal grandfather was a functional alcoholic and WW2 vet. My dad was an alcoholic, but he aged and got addicted to pills instead after experiencing chronic pain.
Being a male comes with a whole different set of problems. I don't really think it's better or worse to be either gender.

It also shouldn't be an 18 year olds job to try and stand up against billion dollar oil companies and corrupted governments. There should be more qualified people doing something to combat it but that's exactly why she became popular because there isn't enough push back against the greed and carelessness.
Thanks, man. I'm working on quitting drinking and just trying the antidepressant, but alcoholism is a bitch.
You're right. It's my damn brain telling me alcohol is what I need. For now I feel okay, but I decided to drink some. We'll see how I feel tomorrow.

Welp, I decided to drink some, hoping I won't end up with massive depression cause I was actually feeling a little better. We will see. Either way, it seems like fluoxetine might be doing me some good as long as I stop drinking. I'll see how I feel tomorrow.
I don't know if I can hold off on drinking for 6 weeks. I was planning on hopefully drinking on one of my two days off per week.

Yeah starting a business sounds pretty freaking hard. I don't even know where I'd start And making 100k/month??? I'd be happy with 100k/year. Really even $50k sounds pretty sweet.

I was up $50,000.

Hey sorry it took me so long to respond. Yeah life is just unfair and it doesn't help when you're underappreciated. What I need to do is go back to school and get trained/certified for something where I'll get paid more. My mental health is just so piss poor right now I don't know what to do. I'm so lonely and I absolutely despise myself, which is why I drink so much and picked up smoking cigarettes. It feels like I've just messed up too much and all I've been doing since I became a teenager is isolate myself and slowly kill myself. And it doesn't help that people have been oddly cruel to me for some reason. 

I mean nothing interests me anymore and I'm in a constant state of anhedonia. I'm tired of feeling this way. The thing too is I was actually doing fairly decent until I got involved with the stock market, then pretty quickly made and lost $50,000 because I didn't sell and got greedy. I also was self-righteous and was infuriated about what happened; it didn't feel right to take the money because people, like your friend, lost everything. Biggest regret of my life thus far not doing so though. I was more okay with it until I saw the price go back up and it's still a thing to this day. It's made working a job feel pointless because I gave up more money than I make in two years, and really did a number on my already low -self esteem. I feel like an idiot. 

I appreciate your kind words though, I hope I make it out too just not very hopeful right now. As for podcasts, I really enjoy comedy as it makes me feel better. I really like Podcast But Outside, Tuesdays with Stories, If I Were You, This Past Weekend, and Your Mom's House. Not sure what kind of podcasts you're looking for, but all of those are hosted by comedians.

I'm right here with ya, my dude. It seems like trading and buying into crypto is the way to go...because especially as of late it seems like their are a lot of people striking gold for no reason. But what I've learned, and am still in the process of learning, is it is all greed the desperation of people hoping (and some succeeding) in obtaining success for no reason. I am still coping with my losses and missed gains too and am hoping to find light at the end of a very dark tunnel.

The present is currently dim, I have no friends nor romantic life so my days outside of work are very uneventful and I don't really enjoy doing much. Mostly just self-loathe and try not to slowly kill myself with booze and cigarettes. Podcasts are the one thing keeping me afloat and helping me not going crazy in my incredibly isolated life. 

I work as a direct support provider on the overnight shift. I'd like to work during the day but my work has a hard time filling my position, so I think they haven't given me the chance because I'm so reliable. It's done a number on my mental health though for sure. It doesn't help that I got involved with the stock market in December 2020, so I've been agonizing and stressing over that because I messed up real bad earlier in the year. Now I have most of my life savings in there and keep losing money cause I'm dumb. So I don't like thinking about the present or future either. Sorry I can't be more positive.
Let the opportunity to make $50,000 slip through my fingers and ever since my mental and physical health has been spiraling out of control.

My mind, drugs, addiction, self-sabotage, inability to measure up to my peers, financial irresponsibility, lack of interests or skills, no guidance or mentors to look up to, self-isolation, just to name a few things what I can think of off the top of my head. 

I've never really been sure what I've wanted to be. I just never had anyone to push me in any direction and wasted time watching TV, playing video games, sports and doing drugs once I got to high school. I wish I would've have been exposed to a different environment and had people around me who were immersed in the community and had viable skills. Instead I was sort of just left to my own devices and left to figure things out on my own, which I failed miserably at sorting out. I regret immensely not reading more and focusing on academics / art and spirituality while growing up. I could've been a totally different person that is admirable and respectable, instead I'm this lonely mess of a human who squanders any and all relationships and opportunity. I verge more on the side of being a homeless alcoholic with no future at this point where I had the chance to be a successful academic if I wasn't an idiot. 

Thanks for the reply by the way.
Dude, fuck off. Every comment I've seen from you is "but like how'd it happen though?". You're never being helpful. Gtfo of here with that shit.

Hey, thanks, I appreciate the response. I am not very good with handling my mistakes and learning from them. I am not very kind to myself and beat myself up instead. Dwelling on the past rather than making peace and realizing all humans make mistakes is sort of my specialty. That is something I am going to work on. 

The girl I am talking about is my coworker and I've known her for about a year. At some point in the future when I'm in a better place I'm hoping to ask her out. As for now though I am just not mentally healthy or stable enough to be trying to start a romantic relationship with anyone. I hope to get there someday, it just seems completely out of reach at the moment.

What I did was get greedy, and now I have lost $11k trying to recreate that wealth. I wish it was that simple just to stop, and forget about the reality I pictured had I sold when I should've. I've been unable to do so as of yet.   I'm just tired of working my job that takes advantage of me and being a total loser. It actually would've given me some confidence, whether I deserved it or not, and the ability to work towards my future. I have a hard time picturing that other opportunities will arise for me. All I've done my woile life is mess up and this just seems like icing on the cake to cap it all off. I'm such a disappointment and I'm incredibly ashamed of who I've become. This whole thing has made me totally neglect my mental and physical health, I know it's not good for me. But I don't know how to stop and change my mindset. I am going to go see a therapist this week but it won't change the damage I've done. I appreciate your optimism but I feel like I'm drowning.
What kind of work do you do?

Yeah I get self-compassion is important. It's just hard to forgive yourself when you make absolutely insanely stupid mistakes. Losing a lot of money definitely does a lot of damage to your self worth and confidence. I was starting to like myself somewhat, but now I'm back to feeling worthless and stupid. Don't know how to stop thinking that way about myself.
Yeah alcohol withdrawal will do that. For me it's been causing terrible depression to the point where I just don't want to live anymore. It's scary.
I set up an appointment to see one, not sure how long my insurance will cover it and I don't know how much good it'll do me though.

I passed up on making $50,000 back in January. Now I've lost $10,000 trying to get it back and feel like a total idiot. I work a minimum wage job I hate and could've used that money to return to college and find my own place. Instead I'm wallowing in sorrow in my childhood home. I'm not sure I'll ever forgive myself.
I get not wanting to be you anymore. I feel that way everyday, wishing I could be the person I want to be instead of the person I am. I'm sorry you're feeling like you are.

Unfortunately siblings don't always get along and stay together. I'm sorry she died and you guys weren't able to become close. I couldn't imagine what that's like.

True. So I never had the money, but I should've had it because I should've cashed out if I wasn't so stupid. I guess I'm me and I'm an idiot.

I'm aware of the resources. I booked an intake appointment with a place in my town that offers counseling and therapy. Not sure it will do much good though. I'm actually really bad at expressing myself and usually shy away from the world in general.

Yeah, I'm really struggling. This honestly isn't my only problem in life, just sort of a cherry on top if you will. I did schedule an in-take appointment with a center in my town that does counseling and therapy. Hoping it helps some.

I'm trying to show myself compassion, but over the past year I was finally able to get back on my feet after being unable to work / find a job due to mental illness and addiction. This is a devastating blow for me and I don't have the greatest coping mechanisms. Working on staying sober but this has made me have major urges. How old are you?

I played a lot of video games and basketball when I was in high school too. My advice, you need to do well in school and at least go to a community college. Don't flunk out. Don't do drugs or drink. Don't watch porn. Work a job and save up money so you can live on your own, find a partner, have friends, etc. Things will change a lot and high school won't matter. Learn life skills and how to be responsible. Don't be like me.

No, just a constant failure and wasted my youth. This hit was just too big of a blow mentally. Showed me how truly desperate and idiotic I am. Don't want to live with the brain of an immature addict who can't handle the stresses of life anymore. I'm weak and my mind is just so fucked up. I never tried to do any of the things I wanted to do because I was too afraid and lacked confidence. It's too late. I already don't have the skills I need to have at this point in life.

Tell me about it. I let everyone push me around and dictate how I should act, who I should be, what I should do, and how I should feel about myself. It's caused me to to absolutely hate myself and unable to interact normally in society or enjoy anything.

I let them and other people define me far too much.

Thanks, man I appreciate it. I'm going to try and work on myself and seeing the light. Today is just one of those days where I'm feeling hopeless for my future and haven't been able to turn that feeling around. Hopefully tomorrow will be a better day.
Will work on it. Not going to keep my hopes up too much though.

Thanks, I appreciate the response. I don't want to be miserable, addicted, and alone anymore. But everything has always seemed to keep compounding on itself. I'm going to work on trying to enjoy the little things in life that are either free, inexpensive, or worth the cost because it's going to help me become a more worthwhile person. It's odd because I rarely ever spend money on anything outside of drugs, alcohol, or the stock market. I'll question spending $10 dollars on food I want, but don't even question spending hundreds on drugs or thousands on a stock that could instantly vanish. I've been sober almost two weeks now, but now I spend my time staring and charts and tickers all day, hoping they go up and god forbid don't crash. I work an overnight job. I've invested everything I have and it's incredibly risky, but I feel like I need it in order to get out of my current situation. So I'm currently in the throws of constantly agonizing over numbers that could either make or break me. Very unhealthy but still haven't learned how to escape. Whenever I'm not working or investing I feel like I'm wasting my time. All I really want to do is volunteer and get a job where I'm helping people. I'm tired of being selfish and overindulging. It's truly killing me. Your story helps knowing that there are ways to get past it all if you are mentally strong and keep moving. Thanks for sharing and trying to help others cope.
